problem: Calling data-parallel training 'SIMD at a larger scale' is loose. Flynn's SIMD means one instruction stream in lockstep over many data lanes, which is what a GPU lane or vector unit does. Separate replicas on separate devices each run their own instruction stream with their own control flow, so the standard label for distributed data parallelism is SPMD (single program, multiple data). A student can carry the wrong definition into a Flynn-taxonomy question.
fix: Say data parallelism is data-level parallelism in the spirit of SIMD; the vector-add case is true SIMD in hardware, but many replicas across devices are SPMD. Adjust the Q2 question or answer to ask for the SIMD link with this qualification.

problem: B_dev = B ÷ P silently assumes the global batch divides evenly by the number of devices. With B = 100 and P = 8 a student gets a fractional 12.5 examples per device and no guidance.
fix: Add: this holds when P divides B; otherwise the last device gets B mod P extra examples, or the batch is padded/dropped so the split is even.
